summary: UI should consume read models for projects, deployments, release channels, route revisions, artifacts, source events, build events, logs, and audit events; the relational control-plane DB is source of truth while artifact storage owns immutable bytes only.

Project list needs GET projects plus global summary and recent events; project detail needs project settings with redacted secret metadata, channels, deployment history, domains, policies, events; deployment detail needs lineage, artifact manifest metadata, route revision, evidence checks, and cursor/paged logs; release console needs candidate/rollback targets, dry-run safety checks, and POST promote/rollback with reason and idempotency key.

Canonical flow is signed webhook -> source_event disposition -> build_job queued/running/succeeded/failed/canceled/timed_out -> artifact uploaded/verified/manifest written -> deployment ready -> release_channel or preview pointer -> pending routing_config_revision -> Nginx validation/apply -> optional CDN operation. UI must never mark deployment routable before verified manifest plus applied route revision.

Use snapshot reads for lists/details, short polling or SSE for active build_events and route revisions, and cursor/range retrieval for logs. Suggested boundaries: project list 15-30s polling, project/deployment detail 5-10s, active build/log/route operations 1-2s or SSE until terminal; CDN status remains separate and retryable after route success.

Plan explicit UI states for no projects, paused project, no deployments, queued build/no worker lease, running build with streaming logs, failed detection/build/publication, verified artifact not routed, route drift, route apply failed with previous known-good preserved, CDN disabled/skipped/failed, and previews present-but-P1-disabled.

Promote/rollback APIs need eligibility checks for successful deployment, verified retained artifact, route dry-run pass, protected previous target, actor, reason, audit event, request/idempotency key, and explicit outcome. Secrets must be redacted from project reads, webhook rejection records, logs, manifests, route config, and UI copies.

Repository root currently contains only .workflow artifacts; no package.json, lockfile, app source, or established frontend conventions were found. The plan should scaffold the UI implementation and treat brainstorm/design-ref artifacts as the source of truth instead of inventing existing patterns.

Shared components should start with AppShell, SidebarNav, Topbar, Panel, MetricCard, StatusPill, Button, FilterToolbar, DataTable, Timeline, LogPanel, LineageChain, EvidenceTable, RouteRevisionBadge, SafetyChecks, AuditReasonForm, StickyActionBar, EnvironmentMatrix, and ActivityInspector.

Adopt design-tokens.json as generated CSS variables or theme constants: OKLCH colors, Inter/JetBrains Mono, 4/6/8px radii, compact 14px body text, semantic status colors, stable table widths, and animation-tokens reduced-motion rules. Avoid bespoke palette or marketing hero treatment.

Likely scaffold targets: package.json, index.html, src/main.tsx, src/App.tsx, src/styles/tokens.css, src/styles/global.css, src/components/ui/*, src/components/shell/*, src/features/projects/*, src/features/deployments/*, src/features/release/*, src/lib/api.ts, src/lib/fixtures.ts, and tests for components/routes.

Minimal frontend stack recommendation: TypeScript + React + Vite, plain CSS modules or global token CSS, lucide-react for icons, React Router for four console routes, Vitest/Testing Library for unit tests, and Playwright for responsive/screenshot smoke tests. Add TanStack Query only when API contracts exist.

Initial implementation can use fixture-backed read models for project list/detail, deployment detail, and release/rollback console while keeping src/lib/api.ts as the data boundary. Verification should include npm run build, npm test, and Playwright checks at mobile and desktop widths for no overlap, horizontal table overflow, sticky actions, and reduced-motion CSS.

data.description: Design artifacts define a shared app shell with sidebar/topbar and four primary operational views: project index, project detail, deployment evidence detail, and release/rollback console.

UI state should follow the canonical lineage source_event -> build_job -> artifact -> deployment -> release_channel or preview_deployment, with DB records as source of truth and artifact storage owning only immutable bytes.

Promotion and rollback screens need a transactional command boundary: validate verified deployment, require audit reason where applicable, move one channel pointer, create channel event and pending route revision, then let route/CDN side effects run through retryable outbox work.

data.naming: Use domain nouns from guidance and feature specs: project, repository_binding, source_event, build_job, artifact, deployment, release_channel, route_revision, channel_event, audit_event.
data.imports: UI should import design tokens from design-ref/design-tokens.json and animation-tokens.json; avoid inventing implementation tokens.
data.formatting: Operations Ledger shell: dense tables, stable columns, status pills, inspector rails, dark monospace logs, reduced-motion support, no marketing hero or nested decorative cards.

data.risk: Secrets and provider payloads could leak through project settings, webhook diagnostics, build logs, manifests, route config, UI fixtures, or copied evidence exports.
data.mitigation: Use secret metadata/read models only, central redaction helpers, canary-string fixture tests, safe rejection summaries, and automated checks that rendered DOM/log fixtures never expose raw secret-like values.

data.risk: Promote and rollback controls move production/staging traffic and can be executed with insufficient context if they look like ordinary buttons.
data.mitigation: Require verified deployment eligibility, protected rollback target, visible current-vs-next channel delta, mandatory audit reason, disabled action until safety checks pass, idempotency key, and confirmation that names channel, target, actor, and route consequence.

data.risk: Deployment, release channel, route revision, and CDN operation states can become stale or partially successful, causing UI to show routed/healthy before side effects finish or after route drift appears.
data.mitigation: Model route revision and CDN status separately from deployment success; show pending/applied/failed/drift states; use polling or SSE for active builds/routes; include last-updated timestamps and stale-data indicators.

data.risk: Route reload failure semantics are ambiguous after channel pointer commit: Nginx/CDN side effects may fail while database state changes succeed.
data.mitigation: Expose channel event outcome plus routing_config_revision outcome; avoid labeling an operation fully complete until route apply succeeds; provide retry/compensating rollback affordances and preserve previous known-good route evidence.

data.risk: Operations Ledger density can hurt accessibility on mobile: horizontal tables, sticky action bars, icon-only controls, log panels, and status colors can impair keyboard, screen reader, and touch use.
data.mitigation: Add accessible names, visible focus states, non-color status text, logical headings, skip navigation, keyboard table/log access, sticky bars that do not overlap content, and mobile/desktop a11y plus screenshot checks.

data.risk: Artifact retention and rollback safety can be misrepresented if UI lists expired, delete-pending, unverified, or unprotected artifacts as selectable known-good targets.
data.mitigation: Rollback selector must filter or clearly disable failed/unverified/expired/deleted-artifact deployments, show retention/protection status, and require backend eligibility checks again at command submission.

data.risk: No implementation baseline exists, so plan tasks can miss regression coverage for redaction, destructive actions, stale state, responsive overflow, reduced motion, and route-state copy.
data.mitigation: Make tests first-class in the scaffold: Vitest/Testing Library for guards and rendered states, Playwright for 375/768/1280 widths, axe/a11y checks if available, and build checks for reduced-motion CSS and no secret canaries.

data.risk: Plan collision risk is high because the repository has no source tree or git metadata; multiple future tasks could scaffold or edit the same package, app shell, token CSS, and fixture/API files.
data.mitigation: Assign one scaffold owner for package/build/tokens/shell, keep route feature tasks on distinct feature folders, list exact file ownership in TASK files, use specific file staging only, and note that commit-oriented steps require repository initialization first.
